passages.provision_quote: On and after January 1, 2025, an agency responsible for the development or operation of bikeways or highways where bicycle travel is permitted shall not install a new sharrow on a highway that has a posted speed limit greater than 30 miles per hour, except at or near an intersection for the purpose of connecting a Class I, Class II, or Class IV bikeway through the intersection.
passages.note: SB 1216 restricts sharrow installation on fast roads and bars Class III bikeways from the Active Transportation Program, a bikeway design/safety standard for how cyclists share the road, not a statement on the road-vs-multimodal investment split.

rows.reasoning: The only source is SB 1216 (2023-2024), which Blakespear authored, restricting new sharrow markings on highways over 30 mph and removing Class III bikeways from Active Transportation Program eligibility. This matches the annex's own hard case that a law about how cyclists share the road is a safety/design standard, not evidence of where transportation investment is focused, so it cannot establish any rung of 'Where should government focus its transportation investment?'
needs_source: A record or own-words statement by Blakespear that addresses the split between road capacity investment and multimodal (transit, bike, pedestrian) investment, e.g. a vote or statement on funding allocation, a road-diet/lane-reduction measure, or a highway-expansion vote
